extracted.intended_audience: members of the public, advocates, and organizations preparing public (notice-and-comment) regulatory submissions
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and a reusable template for drafting effective public comments on proposed regulations, focusing on structure, evidence, and agency-relevant requests. Targets commenters who want to submit substantive, non-duplicative input to administrative dockets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Basic three-part structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Public comments are generally composed of: 1) An introduction - identification, credentials, statement of interest; 2) A reaction to the proposed law - detailing what sections should be kept, removed, or altered and why; 3) An overall summary or conclusion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this high-level structure to organize your comment so agencies can quickly see who you are, what you are commenting on, and the concrete action you want. The template example follows this exact flow and places detailed supporting material between the reaction and the summary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Introduction: identification, credentials, and statement of interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Introduce yourself in 1-2 sentences: who you are and your credentials as they relate to the comment you are writing (e.g., 'I am... [1-2 sentences introducing yourself and your credentials, as they relate to the comment you are writing]').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Opening sentence should establish credibility—state who you are and summarize relevant experiences. Keep the intro concise and directly tied to why your perspective matters to the docket.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reaction to the proposed law with specific recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: State your substantive position and why: 'I would like to... [raise concerns / inform you of new information / provide supporting evidence] regarding [Document Title].' Detail what sections should be kept, removed, or altered and why.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When criticizing or supporting provisions, use specific section references and explain the rationale. Provide concrete alternative language or edits where possible to make it easy for the agency to act on your suggestion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use specific section references
rubrics_metrics.description: When commenting on a particular provision, reference the exact section or regulatory citation (e.g., section number, paragraph).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Precise citations demonstrate careful review and let agency staff map your comment to the proposed text; they reduce ambiguity and increase the chance of actionable consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organize supporting points into major points with short paragraphs
rubrics_metrics.description: [First major point] Several short paragraphs supporting your first point. [Second major point] Several short paragraphs supporting your second point. Include references to literature that is cited in the bibliography.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Break the body into clearly labeled major points. Use several short paragraphs per point and include citations to relevant literature or evidence. This makes the comment scannable and easier for reviewers to parse and cite.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cite sources and include a bibliography
rubrics_metrics.description: BIBLIOGRAPHY: List of your sources; include links or DOI when appropriate. Cite sources for any factual claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support factual claims with citations (studies, reports, data). Provide a bibliography with links or DOIs so agency staff can verify and follow up. Well-documented evidence strengthens credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conclusion: concise summary and clear ask
rubrics_metrics.description: In summary, [1-2 sentences summarizing your comment]. Conclude with a clear ask—what action should the agency take.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: End with a brief recap and an explicit request (e.g., adopt X change, delete Y provision, conduct more study). A clear ask makes it easier for the agency to translate your comment into regulatory action or a response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include heading with regulation name and docket ID
rubrics_metrics.description: Heading with regulation name and docket ID number - demonstrates careful review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place the regulation name and docket ID prominently at the top of your comment so it is correctly filed to the intended rulemaking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personalization and local impact details
rubrics_metrics.description: Strong templates leave space for substantive customization: Personal experience field; Specific section citations; Local impact details; Quantitative data fields.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide personal anecdotes, local impacts, and quantitative data where relevant. Tailoring the comment to your experience and locality reduces duplication and increases persuasiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid high-duplicate-risk (weak) templates
rubrics_metrics.description: Weak templates (high duplicate risk): Pre-filled positions only; No engagement with specific provisions; No personalization mechanism; One-click submission with identical text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid submitting or endorsing boilerplate-only, pre-filled comments. Templates should allow for customization; identical mass-submissions are less persuasive and flagged as duplicates. Ensure engagement with particular provisions and include unique, substantive content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concise intro and summary length
rubrics_metrics.description: Template recommends brief framing: 1-2 sentences for introduction and 1-2 sentences for the summary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep the opening and closing concise so reviewers can quickly grasp your identity and principal ask; reserve detail for the supporting sections and bibliography.
